key_insight: EPPC-CARE identifies communication behaviors in patient-provider messages through staged annotation, linking each label to supporting text for review.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support larger-scale research on patient-provider communication and human-in-the-loop annotation workflows.
method: Sequentially identifies text spans, broad communication codes, and specific subcodes.
Evaluates annotation triplets across six open-weight language models.
Compares performance with supervised fine-tuning, EPPC-OASIS, and human expert annotations.
evidence_signal: Across 867 messages with 5,516 reference annotations, EPPC-CARE improved Triplet F1 over EPPC-OASIS by an average of 2.90 percentage points, reaching a best score of 64.4%; agreement with the reference standard was comparable to a human expert on 100 messages.
watch_item: Performance on these evaluated messages does not establish generalizability across health systems; annotation errors remain a concern requiring human review.
paper_title: EPPC-CARE: Staged Hierarchical Annotation of Communication Behaviors in Secure Patient-Provider Messages
